baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causative يُدْخِلُ with فِي makes mercy an entered domain, while the fronted وَٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ opens the opposed prepared-punishment clause.
baseline_models.mechanism: Divine willing assigns two unlike outcomes: admission into an encompassing mercy, or a deliberately readied pain for those marked by withholding right.

activation_trace.role: Literal entry into an inside gives mercy the functional shape of a destination.
Will directed toward bringing about a thing governs the admission.
Tenderness and beneficence identify the entered domain as active care.
Withholding or confining another from a right supplies the opposed human disposition.
Preparing provisions for a coming event makes punishment readied rather than improvised.
Severe infliction and penalty fix the adverse outcome as punishment.
The pain-causing description blocks any neutral reading of that prepared outcome.

changed_reading.before: A general promise of mercy followed by a general threat.
changed_reading.after: A two-destination allocation: caused entry into active care versus a pain already provisioned for rights-withholders.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction يُدْخِلُ ... فِي رَحْمَتِهِ joins literal inward entry to a root inventory containing kinship and the womb.
baseline_models.mechanism: The locative construction lets mercy be more than an attitude: it can be carried as a protective, life-giving interior and a relation of belonging.

activation_trace.role: Entry into an inside supplies the spatial operation.
Near kinship gives the interior a relation of belonging.
The womb as a containing place of growth supplies the life-bearing interior image.

changed_reading.before: Mercy is favor bestowed on someone who remains outside it.
changed_reading.after: Mercy can be read as a protective belonging into which a person is brought and within which life is sustained.

context_deltas.mechanism: The early أَعْتَدْنَا and final أَعَدَّ share the preparation branch, so the close retrieves an adverse provision announced near the opening and presents it as continuously ready.

activation_trace.role: Something present and prepared makes the opening punishment inventory already at hand.
The mapped preparation-of-provision branch directly links the opening verb to the focus verb.
The focus repeats the preparing operation and closes the frame.

structural_cues: 76:4 announces prepared chains, fetters, and blaze; 76:31 ends with prepared painful punishment.
Both clauses pair a marked wrong group with first-person or divine preparation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two preparation forms and parallel penal recipients; I infer a framing return that makes the final penalty longstanding, while a live alternative is ordinary repeated diction without a deliberate inclusio.

changed_reading.before: The final punishment sounds like a fresh verdict at the close.
changed_reading.after: The close recalls the punishment provision announced at 76:4: it has stood prepared across the surah's intervening alternatives.

context_deltas.mechanism: A person wills and takes a path, that willing is nested under divine willing, and the divine will is named knowing and wise immediately before the focus repeats 'whom He wills.' Admission therefore closes a staged agency sequence rather than appearing as an isolated choice formula.

activation_trace.role: Human willing initiates the local path-taking construction.
A traversable extended path gives willing an enacted direction.
The paired willing forms explicitly nest human willing within divine willing.
Disclosure to the knower qualifies the governing will with knowledge.
Right-judging wisdom qualifies the governing will as purposive.
The focus repetition applies that just-qualified will to admission into mercy.

structural_cues: 76:29-31 forms an uninterrupted sequence of human willing, divine willing, and divine admission.
The path object in 76:29 lies between the two levels of willing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated will syntax, path, knowledge, and wisdom; I infer that the sequence locally qualifies admission as purposeful and responsive to path-taking, while it remains possible that knowledge and wisdom describe divine willing without disclosing any admission criterion.

changed_reading.before: 'Whom He wills' is an opaque, context-free selection.
changed_reading.after: It is the terminal divine act in a layered agency sequence: a taken path, human will under divine will, and a will explicitly marked knowing and wise.

context_deltas.mechanism: Protection, a tree-covered garden, flowing springs, direct watering, and a drink that purifies turn the baseline interior of mercy into a sustained habitat whose boundaries protect and whose provisions transform entrants.

activation_trace.role: Ward-off protection supplies the habitat's protective boundary.
A garden covered by trees gives the protected interior a concrete setting.
A flowing water source makes provision internal and renewable.
Giving drink makes care personally administered within the setting.
A purifier that cleanses another makes the provision transformative, not merely decorative.
Caused inward entry binds the reward landscape back to the focus construction.
Active tenderness and beneficence name the habitat's governing quality.

structural_cues: The reward sequence repeatedly locates recipients 'in it' and surrounds them with shade, vessels, springs, clothing, and drink.
76:31's فِي resumes the reward section's repeated interior grammar.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a protected, provisioned reward topology and the focus supplies entry 'into' mercy; I infer that the topology realizes mercy as an environment, while the alternative is that these are adjacent rewards rather than a definition of mercy.

changed_reading.before: Mercy is an abstract favorable disposition.
changed_reading.after: Mercy is also an inhabitable regime of protection, renewable provision, and purification into which one is admitted.

context_deltas.mechanism: People feed exposed dependents while refusing repayment or thanks; God later repays them and declares their striving thanked. Mercy thus reads as the divine return of care that was deliberately given without a return, opposed by the focus image of withholding right.

activation_trace.role: Feeding another supplies the initiating, outward movement of care.
Reciprocal recompense is explicitly declined from the human recipient.
Acknowledgment of benefit is likewise declined, making the care unpriced.
Divine recompense reverses the earlier refusal of human recompense.
Earned action identifies the sustained conduct being answered.
Divine acknowledgment returns the thanks the caregivers did not demand.
Beneficent tenderness names the divine side of this returned care.
Withholding right provides the exact relational counter-mechanism.

structural_cues: 76:9's rejected جَزَاء and شُكُور return positively in 76:12 and 76:22.
The cared-for figures in 76:8 are socially exposed: needy person, orphan, and captive.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a refusal-and-return pattern for recompense and thanks; I infer that entry into mercy is the divine completion of that care circuit and that ظلم breaks it by withholding right, while the alternative is a looser juxtaposition of conduct and reward.

changed_reading.before: Mercy and punishment classify isolated individuals.
changed_reading.after: Mercy completes a relational economy in which unpriced care is returned by God, while wrongdoing is the withholding that opposes that circulation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because عَذَاب plainly denotes punishment here, yet its inventory also carries sweet water and withholding; it remains anchored by عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا and the context's dense drink field. Render only as a secondary material counter-reading, never as a replacement for painful punishment.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: عَذَابًا combines branches of potable sweetness, withholding, and punishment, while أَلِيمًا decisively preserves pain.

activation_trace.role: Sweet, palatable water supplies the lexical counter-image to punishment.
Restraint, prevention, or weaning supplies deprivation as the proposed punitive mechanism.
Infliction and penalty keep the surface punitive sense controlling.
Pain-causing force contains the wordplay and prevents euphemistic reversal.
The flowing spring supplies what punitive deprivation would exclude.
Being given drink marks participation in the mercy-side flow.
The drink's power to purify makes exclusion a loss of transformation as well as refreshment.

changed_reading.before: Punishment is only positive infliction of pain.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, its pain also includes being withheld or weaned from the sweet, flowing, purifying provision that fills the mercy-side interior.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain reading is surprising because رَحْمَة does not simply mean womb in the focus. It remains anchored in the packet's ر ح م womb branch, literal entry syntax, and the opening creation sequence; downstream prose should call it a possible gestational echo, not a lexical gloss or doctrinal claim.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: يُدْخِلُ ... فِي رَحْمَتِهِ permits literal inward motion, and the ر ح م inventory includes the womb as a life-bearing container.

activation_trace.role: Origination of a creature supplies the opening generative event.
The drop extending to generative fluid gives that event its contained material beginning.
Mixed generative fluid specifies the opening formation process.
Entry into an inside supplies the closing movement into containment.
The womb as a house and growth vessel supplies the possible second generative enclosure.

changed_reading.before: The surah begins with biological creation and ends with unrelated pardon.
changed_reading.after: As a contained echo, entry into mercy can close the opening creation scene as a second, transformative gestation into protected life.

strongest_changes: The final prepared punishment closes the preparation frame opened at 76:4.
The focus will clause culminates 76:29-30's path and nested-willing sequence under knowledge and wisdom.
The reward interior makes mercy spatial: protected, provisioned, and purifying.
The refused-then-returned recompense and thanks recast mercy as God's completion of unpriced care.
summary.what_was_special: The context did not force one gloss; it activated a preparation frame, a layered agency sequence, a material mercy habitat, and a social return mechanism. The womb and sweet-water branches then preserved two unusual but visibly anchored secondary readings.
remaining_uncertainties: The ع ت د/ع د د preparation echo may be framing or simply recurrent penal diction.
The reward landscape may instantiate mercy without exhausting what mercy means.
The deprivation and gestation readings remain branch-level echoes and should not control a synthesis.
